target_customer: Individuals and creators with large personal file libraries
problem: Personal files are scattered and hard to search; desktop file managers lack natural language and multimodal search.
business_model: Freemium cloud storage subscription (100GB free, paid tier at $10 per month for 2TB per TechCrunch snippet)
product_category: AI cloud file storage and browser

founders.name: Abhay Agarwal
previous_startups: Polytopal (AI consultancy, per a secondary source)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder. A TechCrunch snippet says Sam Young was a co-founder who has since left; not on the YC page, so not listed as a founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Multimodal embedding search across text, images, audio and video, plus a performant native feel file browser; the company built its own embedding model (Polyembed-v1).

defensibility.rationale: Storage giants can add AI search; the file browser UI and indexing quality are the only visible edge and Launch HN commenters were skeptical about replacing their file browser.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet shown; Poly relaunched in November 2025 and no incumbent response was found.

market_need_then: In 2022 the original idea was an AI 3D asset generator, with no demand evidence opened. The 2025 pivot followed user interviews that found organizing files was a big unmet need, per TechCrunch coverage.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, confident, concise; The Intelligent File Browser

branding.brand_signature: Launch HN title: Cursor for Files
branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN thread in November 2025 with mixed, skeptical reaction.

brand_strength.rationale: The name collides with HP Poly, Google Poly and others, so search confusion is likely; the Cursor for Files framing helped explain the product.

pivots.why: Team shut the earlier iteration in 2023, went into stealth, and chose file organization after user interviews, per TechCrunch coverage

outcome_analysis: Poly started in YC in 2022 with an AI 3D asset product, shut that iteration in 2023, then relaunched in November 2025 as an AI file browser with an $8M seed led by Felicis. It is early after the relaunch, with a strong investor group but a crowded storage market and skeptical early user reaction.
notes: Seed of $8M in November 2025 confirmed by Pulse 2.0 and GamesBeat (TechCrunch also covered). CB Insights lists an $8M seed dated June 2024 and $12.4M total over five rounds, and one search summary mentions an initial $3.9M raised around December 2022; these are unverified and conflict, so no earlier round is recorded. The 2022 era product (AI 3D assets) had no competitor source dated near the batch opened, so competitors are empty.
